finite_default_domain.definition: Nine seed positions times nine non-background colours: 81.
finite_default_domain.scope: Default native parameter distribution only; finite input count is not inflated by repeated sampling.

provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The constructor draws a square spiral in the 9x9 output. The spiral starts at the anchor (4*row, 4*col), which is the seed's position scaled up. Its segments go in the order up, right, down, left. Segment lengths are 2,2,4,4,6,6,... and each segment paints `length` cells, counting the start cell but not the end cell. Cells off the grid are not painted. This is the same as the archived description: Chebyshev parity rings plus a colour swap along the diagonal ray (ay-1-k, ax-k). The factory turns the four step vectors into visible coordinates. For d4>=4 it first negates the column component (row reversal). It then rotates each vector clockwise d4%4 times using (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr). The emitted program runs the spiral directly in the visible grid with these constant directions, so the reflected cases turn the other way. The anchor scaling 0/1/2 -> 0/4/8 is unchanged by D4, so the anchor is computed from the visible seed position. The background is the constant palette[0]. The seed colour is read from the one non-background cell, so the program does not depend on which colour the seed has. The output is filled with palette[0], and the seed colour is painted along the spiral.
draft_notes.limitations: This has not been run or tested. It assumes the constructor's domain: a 3x3 input holding exactly one non-background cell, producing a 9x9 output. For other sizes it falls back to a 3x scale with an anchor at y*(H-1)/(h-1), and the number of segments grows so the spiral still covers the grid. That fallback goes beyond what the generator defines. It assumes common.draw skips coordinates outside the grid; the approved fixtures and the archived ring-plus-ray solver both agree with that. The fixtures fit a single uniform rule, and I found no contradictions or tie-break defects. The 20-segment spiral is long enough to cover the whole 9x9 grid from any anchor.
